app.title: Veridalis
app.summary: A person uploads a species survey table or a raw occurrence export, or starts with the built-in demonstration survey. The tool maps the columns to standard occurrence terms, flags records with missing or invalid coordinates or a missing taxon, and shows how many records can be used. It computes diversity indices for each site and for the whole survey. It draws each site on a map coloured by diversity class, and flags sites that fall below the person's thresholds for diversity and species richness. The person reads the site table, filters the species records by habitat, and generates a plain-text screening report that they can download or open as a draft email.

task.text: Clean a species survey and screen its sampling sites by diversity indices against adjustable thresholds, ending in a written screening report.

data.text: Species occurrence or abundance records with site coordinates, species names, counts and optional habitat and date, grouped into sampling sites.
data.item: a species count recorded at a sampling site

stage.text: analysing field survey records for site diversity after collection, before detailed modelling

mechanism.text: Upload and threshold sliders in the sidebar drive everything at once. Uploads pass through a quality check whose counts appear as summary stats, while the indices feed a headline row, a clustered map coloured by diversity class and a site table with flags. A report button turns the current metrics and thresholds into text that can be downloaded or emailed.

field.text: biodiversity indices for site survey data in community ecology

workflow.name: compute a metric per site, flag sites below thresholds, and report

steps.here: Upload a CSV or tab-separated file (a GBIF export works too). Without one, a synthetic demonstration survey is used, and a CSV template can be downloaded.

Columns are mapped to Darwin Core terms. Records with missing, zero or out-of-range coordinates or a missing taxon are flagged and dropped, and the raw, flagged and clean counts are shown with a usability score.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Species richness, Shannon–Wiener H′, Simpson 1−D, Pielou J′ and Margalef are computed for each site and for the whole landscape, and each site gets a diversity class from H′ bands.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Sites appear on a clustered map with switchable basemaps. Marker colour shows the diversity class and marker size shows richness, and a popup lists all the indices.

steps.step: flag items that fall below a threshold
steps.here: Sliders set an H′ review threshold and a minimum richness, and each site in the table is marked 'Review suggested' or 'Within screening criteria'.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A habitat multiselect narrows the table of species records.
A button generates a plain-text screening report with scope, data summary, criteria, site metrics, flags and interpretation notes. It can be downloaded as .txt or opened as a Gmail draft.

distinctive: Column names from heterogeneous sources are harmonised to Darwin Core terms, with an audit of how many records can be used
Several diversity indices are computed side by side, with H′ bands mapped to a diversity class and a short rationale
Review thresholds on two separate criteria (H′ and richness) are set live and drive the flags and the report
Map markers encode both diversity class (colour) and species richness (size)
The report carries fixed caveats about sampling effort and pooled taxa
